title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Two Spiritual Mines And The Loss Of Abandoning Prayer

questions.question: What is the first spiritual benefit mentioned for a person who works in a garden with a proper intention?
questions.answer: Such a person gains a share in the worship and praise offered by the plants and trees he raises.

questions.question: According to the passage, what condition is needed to receive that first benefit?
questions.answer: The person must have a sincere and sound intention.

questions.question: What is the second spiritual benefit connected to the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: Whatever is eaten from it can count like charity from the one who worked for it.

questions.question: Which groups are mentioned as eating from the garden’s produce?
questions.answer: People, animals, livestock, flies, customers, and even thieves.

questions.question: What two conditions must be met for what is eaten to count like charity?
questions.answer: The work must be done for Allah, and it must stay within what He has allowed.

questions.question: How should a person view his role in handling the produce?
questions.answer: He should see himself as a servant distributing Allah’s property to His creatures.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person loses by abandoning the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses great spiritual profit and misses the two valuable benefits described earlier.

questions.question: How does leaving the prayers affect a person’s attitude toward work over time?
questions.answer: It weakens his motivation, lowers his morale, and can make him tired of his work.

questions.question: What kind of thinking may develop in a person who becomes spiritually empty in this way?
questions.answer: He may start thinking that effort is pointless since he will leave the world anyway.

questions.question: What negative result can come from that kind of thinking?
questions.answer: He may become lazy and fall into idleness.

questions.question: How is the attitude of the faithful worker different from the idle one?
questions.answer: The faithful worker becomes more eager to combine worship with lawful work.

questions.question: What future goal gives that faithful worker stronger motivation?
questions.answer: He hopes to prepare light for the grave and provisions for the life to come.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the value of growing plants and trees?
questions.answer: It shows that even simple farming work can carry worship-related reward when done rightly.

questions.question: What does the second benefit teach about how a Muslim should think about provision?
questions.answer: It teaches that sustenance ultimately belongs to Allah and reaches His creatures through means He chooses.

questions.question: Why is the worker told to think of himself as a delivery servant rather than an owner?
questions.answer: So he stays humble and recognizes that the real ownership belongs to Allah.

questions.question: What does the mention of thieves suggest about the second benefit?
questions.answer: It suggests that even when produce is taken unexpectedly, reward can still come if the worker’s intention and method were right.

questions.question: How does the passage connect prayer with morale and eagerness?
questions.answer: It presents prayer as something that strengthens a person’s spirit and gives energy for work.

questions.question: What is meant by saying the person who abandons prayer becomes “bankrupt”?
questions.answer: It means he may still work outwardly, but he loses the deeper spiritual profit that gives lasting value.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast two different workers?
questions.answer: One becomes drained and careless without prayer, while the other becomes more purposeful through worship and lawful effort.

questions.question: What does the second worker hope to send ahead through his efforts?
questions.answer: He hopes to prepare brightness for the grave and supplies for the hereafter.

questions.question: What main lesson about dunya and akhirah can be drawn from the whole passage?
questions.answer: A Muslim should not separate daily work from worship, but should use worldly effort to gain eternal reward.

questions.question: What is the main subject of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains spiritual gains connected to lawful work and shows what is lost when prayer is neglected.

questions.question: What specific kind of work is used as the example in the passage?
questions.answer: Working in a garden and growing its produce.

questions.question: What is gained from the first benefit besides the outward harvest?
questions.answer: A share in the remembrance and praise of Allah made by the plants and trees.

questions.question: What transforms food taken from the garden into something like charity?
questions.answer: Working with the right intention, for Allah’s sake, and within halal limits.

questions.question: How does the passage broaden the idea of charity beyond giving money directly?
questions.answer: It shows that even food others eat from your effort can become charity under the right conditions.

questions.question: What belief about ownership is emphasized in the second benefit?
questions.answer: The produce truly belongs to Allah, not absolutely to the human worker.

questions.question: Why does the passage say abandoning prayer leads to a “great loss”?
questions.answer: Because the person gives up major spiritual rewards that could have come from the same work.

questions.question: What happens to a person’s inner state when those rewards are lost?
questions.answer: His motivation weakens and his spirit becomes less steady.

questions.question: How might old age affect the person who works without spiritual purpose?
questions.answer: He may become more tired of his work and less willing to continue it.

questions.question: What sentence best summarizes the hopeless attitude of that person?
questions.answer: He thinks there is no point in struggling since he will leave the world anyway.

questions.question: What attitude does the better example in the passage show?
questions.answer: He chooses to work harder in both worship and lawful earning.

questions.question: Why does that better example continue working with energy?
questions.answer: Because he sees his work as helping him prepare for the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the effect of intention on ordinary daily labor?
questions.answer: It teaches that a good intention can raise ordinary labor into an act with spiritual reward.

questions.question: In the first benefit, whose worship does the worker share in?
questions.answer: He shares in the praise and glorification connected with the plants and trees he cultivates.

questions.question: Does the first benefit depend mainly on the size of the garden or on the state of the heart?
questions.answer: It depends on the state of the heart, especially sincere intention.

questions.question: In the second benefit, what happens when creatures benefit from the garden’s food?
questions.answer: Their eating can count as a charitable reward for the worker.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about serving creation?
questions.answer: Serving creation in a lawful way can become a means of earning reward from Allah.

questions.question: Why must the worker remain within what Allah permits?
questions.answer: Because spiritual reward is tied not only to effort but also to obedience and lawful action.

questions.question: What false attitude is corrected by seeing oneself as a distributor of Allah’s property?
questions.answer: The attitude of acting like one is the absolute owner and source of provision.

questions.question: What is one major effect of neglecting the required prayers according to the passage?
questions.answer: It causes a person to miss the deeper meaning and reward of his work.

questions.question: How does neglect of prayer affect a person’s long-term energy for work?
questions.answer: It can make him discouraged and eventually uninterested in continuing.

questions.question: What kind of statement shows the discouraged worker’s loss of purpose?
questions.answer: He starts acting as if effort no longer matters because this life is temporary.

questions.question: How does the other worker respond to the same reality that this world is temporary?
questions.answer: He uses it as a reason to increase worship and lawful effort for the next life.

questions.question: What overall message does the final contrast between the two workers give?
questions.answer: Prayer gives work meaning, strength, and lasting reward, while leaving prayer empties work of its deeper value.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can a gardener receive from the plants and trees besides material benefit?
questions.answer: He can receive spiritual reward connected to their praise of Allah.

questions.question: What inner quality allows a person to receive that reward?
questions.answer: A sincere and proper intention.

questions.question: What is the second hidden gain found in garden work?
questions.answer: The produce eaten by others can become a form of charity for the worker.

questions.question: Why is it significant that even insects and thieves are mentioned?
questions.answer: It shows the reward can extend very widely to many kinds of consumers, not just expected or welcome ones.

questions.question: What two religious principles control whether this second gain is received?
questions.answer: Intention for Allah and staying within His lawful limits.

questions.question: What view of rizq, or provision, is taught by describing the worker as a distributor?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah is the true giver of provision, while humans only pass it along.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens to the person who gives up the required prayers?
questions.answer: He loses major spiritual wealth and becomes deprived of these two rich benefits.

questions.question: How is that loss described in financial language?
questions.answer: It is described like becoming ruined in wealth.

questions.question: What emotional effect can this spiritual loss have on a person’s work life?
questions.answer: It can drain his enthusiasm and weaken his morale.

questions.question: What kind of lifestyle may follow from that weakening?
questions.answer: A lazy and inactive lifestyle may develop.

questions.question: What makes the second person continue with more determination?
questions.answer: He wants both to worship Allah more and to use lawful work to prepare for the next life.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest is the best way to keep work meaningful until old age?
questions.answer: Join prayer and lawful labor so that work keeps both worldly usefulness and eternal purpose.

questions.question: What two “mines” are described in the passage?
questions.answer: One is sharing in the worship connected to the plants through sincere intention, and the other is receiving charity-like reward from what others eat from the produce.

questions.question: How are these two benefits similar?
questions.answer: Both turn regular garden work into a source of spiritual profit.

questions.question: How are they different from each other?
questions.answer: The first is tied to the existence and growth of the plants, while the second is tied to others benefiting from what is produced.

questions.question: What role does intention play in the first benefit?
questions.answer: It is the key that makes the worker share in that reward.

questions.question: What role does lawful conduct play in the second benefit?
questions.answer: It ensures the benefit is earned in a way pleasing to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about a Muslim’s relationship to property?
questions.answer: A Muslim should not see himself as the ultimate owner, but as a caretaker under Allah’s command.

questions.question: Why does the passage call the loss from leaving prayer a serious one?
questions.answer: Because the person loses hidden treasures of reward that could give his labor eternal value.

questions.question: What practical effect does this loss have on a person’s motivation?
questions.answer: It makes his drive weaker and his spirit less steady.

questions.question: What kind of thoughts may enter the mind of someone who loses that spiritual purpose?
questions.answer: He may begin to think effort is pointless because life in this world does not last.

questions.question: What is the result of such thinking on behavior?
questions.answer: It can lead to laziness and withdrawal from useful effort.

questions.question: What is the attitude of the person who understands these spiritual benefits?
questions.answer: He becomes more committed to both worship and halal work.

questions.question: What final lesson about prayer and labor is taught by the passage?
questions.answer: Prayer does not take away from useful work; it gives that work blessing, purpose, and reward for the hereafter.
